Rina V.: hey team, first-day q: followed onboarding steps but `kubectl get pods -n dev-sandbox` errors with Forbidden. I set context to redwood-dev-central. any quick checks?

Onboarding Bot: welcome Rina! Make sure you completed SSO (redwoodctl login --sso) and then ran redwoodctl sync-kubeconfig. See onboarding page: https://intranet.redwood/dev-onboarding#k8s.

Rina V.: I did SSO. output:
```
kubectl config current-context
# redwood-dev-central
kubectl get pods -n dev-sandbox
# Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User \"system:anonymous\" cannot list resource \"pods\" in API group \"\" in the namespace \"dev-sandbox\"
```

Jorge L.: that anonymous error usually means kubectl is not using your auth token. Quick: `echo $KUBECONFIG` and `kubectl config view --minify --raw` (please redact tokens). Are you merging multiple kubeconfigs?

Rina V.: `echo $KUBECONFIG` -> `/home/rina/.kube/config:/home/rina/.kube/old-config` (I forgot the old one).

Jorge L.: yep. either unset KUBECONFIG or point it to a single file. Try: `unset KUBECONFIG; redwoodctl sync-kubeconfig --cluster=redwood-dev-central; kubectl config use-context redwood-dev-central; kubectl auth can-i get pods -n dev-sandbox`.

Rina V.: did that. `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n dev-sandbox` -> "no". infra-bot created INFRA-10234.

infra-bot: INFRA-10234 created: new-hire RBAC check for rinav. Current: not in group "redwood:devs". Please add GitHub handle to the ticket for automated binding.

Rina V.: added my GitHub handle. small safety q: I have prod contexts in old-config. should I delete them?

Jorge L.: don't delete—move prod contexts to a separate file and do not merge. For safety set default namespace: `kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=dev-sandbox`. Also consider `kubectl config rename-context` to tag prod contexts.

infra-bot: INFRA-10234 updated: applied rolebinding `namespace=dev-sandbox role=edit subject=group:redwood:devs`. Sync in progress (expected ~15m).

Rina V.: ~18m later: `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n dev-sandbox` -> "yes" and `kubectl get pods -n dev-sandbox` works. thanks! added a note to onboarding that KUBECONFIG merging causes most failures.

Jorge L.: welcome aboard! tips: always run `kubectl auth can-i` before destructive commands, use `--dry-run=client` for experiments, and keep prod contexts isolated. ping me for a quick namespace walkthrough.
